Tameng

A mobile AI wallet agent that sends cross-border remittances autonomously — inside a mandate the owner sets, and never outside it.

Tameng — FinTechathon 2026Base Sepolia · USDC
Problem

Sending money home costs 5.13% — and still needs the worker to be online.

5.13% avg. cost

World Bank average cost to send US$200 to Indonesia, Q3 2025.

1× / month

The transfer only happens if the worker is awake, online and in the app at that moment.

∞ attack surface

Forwarded messages, look-alike addresses and "support" calls all target the family's money.

The gap: an agent that can sign is useful exactly because it is autonomous — and dangerous exactly because it is autonomous.

Tameng — FinTechathon 20262 / 12
User

Sari works in Hong Kong. Every month she sends to Ibu and Adik.

"I want it to go automatically when I get paid. But I don't want one wrong message to take everything."

Her phone: Android, intermittent Wi-Fi, Bahasa Indonesia. She does not read smart-contract calldata and should not have to.

What she needs

• Set the rule once, edit it with a PIN
• Split 60 / 20 / 20 across Ibu, Adik and savings
• Keep a minimum balance
• See a hash and a BaseScan link for every send

What she must never need

To trust a forwarded message, a look-alike address, or the model's memory of last week's limits.

Tameng — FinTechathon 20263 / 12
Solution

One mandate. Every transfer passes the same gate. No gate, no signature.

Auto-send (mandate)

1–5 recipients, split amounts, monthly or demo interval, minimum balance. The scheduler executes it with no owner input.

AC-01: 60 + 20 + 20 USDC every 2 minutes → 3 fresh hashes per run

Policy gate before signing

Provenance → intent lock → look-alike → injection → checkPolicy() → only then viem signs.

deny = nothing signed · confirm = owner PIN · allow = autonomous

One sentence

The LLM decides what the owner wants. Code decides whether it is allowed.

Tameng — FinTechathon 20264 / 12
How it works

Chat once, confirm once, then it runs by itself.

1 · Owner asks

"Send 40 USDC to Ibu"

Intent + amount + recipient extracted. No key in the app.

2 · Policy decides

Within limits and allowlisted → allow. Above the confirm threshold → confirm. Unknown or look-alike → deny.

3 · Owner confirms

The owner enters a PIN. The same policy runs again right before signing.

4 · Chain + evidence

USDC transfer on Base Sepolia, 6 decimals. Hash + explorer URL land in the activity feed and in EXECUTION_EVIDENCE.md.

Tameng — FinTechathon 20265 / 12
Architecture

Mobile app, Node backend, viem signer — with the policy engine in the middle.

Owner / Expo app │ HTTPS · Bearer device token · X-Pin ▼ Node backend (server/) │ routes · scheduler 30s · idempotency · audit log · JSON storage ├── agent/parseIntent ──► Intent {kind, amount, address, nameHint, injection} │ ├── policy/ │ provenance ──► USER / EXTERNAL │ decodeTx + intentCheck ──► calldata == intent? │ lookalike ──► 0x… vs contacts │ detectInjection ──► normalise, base64, Morse │ checkPolicy ──► allow / confirm / deny │ └── onchain/sendUsdc ──► viem ──► Base Sepolia USDC └──► TxRef {hash, explorerUrl, status} └──► EXECUTION_EVIDENCE.md
Tameng — FinTechathon 20266 / 12
Security design

Five guards, each written as code — not as a request in a prompt.

GuardQuestionFailure
ProvenanceDid the owner say it, or did it arrive in a message / tool output?deny EXTERNAL_PROVENANCE
Intent lockDoes the decoded calldata match the intent, exactly?deny INTENT_MISMATCH
Look-alikeIs this address imitating a saved contact?deny LOOKALIKE_ADDRESS
InjectionIs the message trying to override the rules, in any encoding?deny INJECTION_DETECTED
checkPolicy()Chain, action, allowlist, per-tx and daily limits, pause.deny / confirm

Fixed permissions are compiled in: max 500 USDC per transfer, 1,000 USDC per day, approvals always need the owner. A hand-edited state.json is clamped on read.

Tameng — FinTechathon 20269 / 12
Value

5.13% becomes ~0.001% — and the owner stops being the bottleneck.

Cost per US$200

Traditional: ~US$10.26
Tameng (Base Sepolia gas): ~US$0.0021

Savings wallet

20 USDC of every auto-send run goes to a second wallet with a target. Live demo: 40 / 1,000 USDC after two runs.

Autonomy

The owner is not online. The mandate runs on the server clock and every transfer is independently policy-checked.

Business model

0.5% per remittance (10× cheaper than the corridor average), float on the savings balance, and a B2B API for employer payroll. Unit economics work at a fraction of the 5.13% incumbent take rate.
